entries.3345bd36ff1eb4f2: A business that explores for non-ferrous metal ores in Japan and overseas, develops mines, and extracts and sells the ore. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥192,448 million (¥141,140 million in the previous year). It is centered on the mining and sale of gold and silver ore and the production and sale of copper concentrate and copper by the SX-EW method, and has consolidated subsidiaries and equity-method companies in the United States, Canada, Chile, Peru, Australia and elsewhere. An overview of the main mines in the fiscal year ended March 2026 is as follows. The Hishikari Mine (Kagoshima Prefecture) sold 3.5 t of gold as planned; the Morenci copper mine (United States) produced 314,000 t, in line with the previous year (the company's interest: 25.0%); the Cerro Verde copper mine (Peru) produced 391,000 t, below the previous year owing to a decline in ore feed grade and other factors (same, 16.8%); the Quebrada Blanca copper mine (Chile) produced 183,000 t, below the previous year owing to a temporary constraint on the processing capacity of the tailings storage facility (same, 25.0%); and the Cote gold mine (Canada) produced 12.4 t, above plan (same, 30.0%). The company's interest is the percentage excluding non-controlling interests. The average prices of copper and gold in the same period were above the previous year. The company purchases copper concentrate from Sumitomo Metal Mining Arizona Inc., SMM Morenci Inc., Compania Contractual Minera Candelaria, Sociedad Minera Cerro Verde and others.

entries.4581a2839dc00be4: Its long-term vision is to be the world leader in nonferrous metals, and it sets out, among other things, having a global presence in resource interests and metal production volumes (metals in the world Top5), and places as targets nickel production of 150,000 tons per year, copper production on an equity basis of 300,000 tons per year, new participation in mine operations through acquisition of quality gold interests, and profit attributable to owners of parent of ¥150 billion per year. The Medium-Term Management Plan 2027 (fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2027), announced in May 2025, is positioned as a critical juncture toward realizing this long-term vision. Its basic strategies include responding to changes in the business environment (making the Quebrada Blanca copper mine and the Côté gold mine operational, rebuilding the battery materials business, strengthening the competitiveness of the smelting business, and business portfolio management) and preparing for the next growth (advancing the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project - Goongarrie Hub and the Winu copper-gold project, a lithium-ion secondary battery recycling business, SiC bonded substrates, and near-infrared absorbing materials).

entries.638bb19cefbf8a34: This business makes and sells materials used in batteries and electronic components. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥249,585 million (¥268,037 million in the previous fiscal year). Battery materials nickel hydroxide and lithium nickelate are used in positive electrodes of batteries, including those for vehicles. Other products include powder materials (paste, nickel powder, near-infrared absorbing materials and magnetic materials), crystal materials (such as lithium tantalate substrates) and package materials (tape materials, printed wiring boards and others). The company also handles lubricants and catalysts (automotive exhaust gas treatment catalysts, chemical catalysts and petroleum refining desulfurization catalysts). The company combines the battery materials business and the functional materials business into one reportable segment, as their nature and target customers are similar. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, demand for automotive battery materials grew moderately compared with the previous year, while components for electronic parts recovered, led by demand related to data centers and semiconductors. Major customers Panasonic Holdings Corporation and Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. are shown in the filing as related to both the "Smelting" and "Materials" reportable segments.

entries.7bcad0d39edbd2c4: Consolidated net sales in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥1,741,586 million, up 9.3% from the previous fiscal year (¥1,593,348 million). The increase was due to factors such as the average prices of copper, gold and other metals exceeding those of the previous fiscal year, and the effect of foreign exchange, with the yen weakening from the middle of the period. The average price of copper rose from $9,370 per 1 ton in the previous fiscal year to $10,816, gold rose from $2,584.7 per 1 troy ounce to $3,939.1, and nickel fell from $7.51 per 1 pound to $7.08. Net sales to external customers by [[term:segment|reporting segment]] were Smelting ¥1,296,277 million, Materials ¥249,585 million, and Resources ¥192,448 million, and “Others,” which is not included in the reporting segments, was ¥3,276 million. In Resources and Smelting, fluctuations in nonferrous metal prices and foreign exchange rates, and in Materials, changes in market trends, are cited as the main factors that have an important effect on business results.

entries.832439212dc61bca: This business extracts metals from ore and concentrates and sells them as metal products such as copper, nickel, zinc and precious metals. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,296,277 million (¥1,180,248 million in the previous fiscal year), the largest of the four segments (consolidated revenue was ¥1,741,586 million). Products are smelted products such as copper, nickel, ferronickel and zinc, and precious metals such as gold, silver, platinum and palladium. The company's main product production volumes were 412,591 t of copper (442,960 t in the previous fiscal year), 66,155 t of electrolytic nickel (60,108 t in the previous fiscal year), 4,800 t of ferronickel (3,317 t in the previous fiscal year) and 14,261 kg of gold (18,709 kg in the previous fiscal year), and production volumes include amounts under consignment processing and entrustment. Copper fell below the previous year because of the periodic furnace relining (major shutdown) at the Toyo Works, while electrolytic nickel reached its highest production volume ever. In Japan, Hyuga Smelting Co., Ltd., Shikama Smelting Co., Ltd. and others are consolidated subsidiaries, and in the Philippines, Coral Bay Nickel Corporation and Taganito HPAL Nickel Corporation are consolidated subsidiaries; the company purchases nickel raw materials from these two companies. Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo K.K. is linked to this segment as a major customer, with revenue of ¥175,114 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026. Panasonic Holdings Corporation and Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. are also major customers, but the filing shows their related reportable segments as both "Smelting" and "Materials".
